generated.title: M6.9 Earthquake Strikes Vanuatu, Second M6.3 Follows Minutes Later
generated.description:
A magnitude 6.9 earthquake struck 197 km west-northwest of Port-Olry, Vanuatu, on October 24, 2026 at 02:31 UTC, at a depth of 10 km, according to the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). The event data has been reviewed by USGS.

A second earthquake, magnitude 6.3 (USGS event us6000u4jb, https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/us6000u4jb), was recorded about 4.5 minutes later, at 02:35 UTC, 170 km northwest of Port-Olry at a depth of 10 km. Its magnitude is a body-wave (mb) value and may be revised.

Both earthquakes are part of a sequence northwest of Port-Olry. USGS also recorded a magnitude 6.0 earthquake on October 19 (us6000u3bc, https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/us6000u3bc) and a magnitude 6.3 earthquake on October 20 (us6000u3jl, https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/us6000u3jl), along with several earthquakes of magnitude 5 and above in the area.

USGS issued a green PAGER alert for the magnitude 6.9 earthquake. PAGER is a modeled estimate of potential fatalities and economic losses, not a report of what actually happened.

The USGS record carries a tsunami flag for this event. That flag is a general indicator and is not a confirmation that a tsunami occurred. In the information we reviewed, no tsunami impacts, casualties or damage have been confirmed. This may change as more information becomes available.

Magnitude is the USGS value (Mww). Other agencies may publish different preliminary magnitudes for the same earthquake.

Official event page: https://earthquake.usgs.gov/earthquakes/eventpage/us6000u4j2
